analysis: Both supplied units are BASE text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (lines 1237-2116). Only a truncated patch excerpt is available, and the changed ranges fall outside the supplied base excerpts (the earliest changes are at line 1035 and the supplied base text begins at 1237). The visible patch shows the --linux-slots/--macos-slots row now says counts above the estimate are taken as-is and shown as '(your choice)', where before they were 'flagged, not refused'. This is a documentation description of CLI behavior. If the code now stops flagging over-estimate slot counts, that is an availability/local-resource matter for the owner's own Mac, and the supplied evidence does not show any boundary crossing. The Setup step 1 rewrite removes the chip/memory/disk/cores checks from the printed output and adds a 'Not eligible' refusal table. I could not verify whether the underlying code (SandboxAddon, installer) actually dropped those checks. Relevant threat entries are TB-013/T-061 (installer download and run as the Mac owner) and T-059/T-060 (add-on hold). The docs in the supplied base text still describe the add-on runtime directory, owner-only sockets and the add-on command as the owner. The truncated patch does not show any change to the installer trust model, such as HTTPS-only server validation or integrity checks on install.sh. A next pass should confirm that the head Setup text (head lines ~1050-1071) does not weaken documented guarantees for TB-013, for example by dropping the https/no-credentials constraint on --server or the confirmation step. No concrete security regression is supported by the supplied evidence.
